metadata.description: Drop-in behavioral detection and response platform for Node.js/Express applications
metadata.author: GhostTrace Team

overview.summary: GhostTrace is an enterprise-grade security monitoring and threat detection platform that integrates into any Node.js/Express application with minimal code. It provides real-time behavioral analysis, anomaly detection, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and AI-powered threat triage through a dedicated SOC dashboard.

issue.problem: Port already in use error on startup

symptoms.symptom: Error: Port 3001 is already in use

causes.cause: Another process is using the dashboard port
Previous GhostTrace instance didn't shut down cleanly

solutions.solution: Set different port: GHOST_PORT=4001 in .env or pass dashboardPort: 4001 to init()
Find and kill process using port: lsof -ti:3001 | xargs kill -9
Restart your machine to clear all ports
Verify database is running: pg_isready (PostgreSQL) or mysql status
Check credentials in .env: GHOST_DB_USER, GHOST_DB_PASS
GhostTrace will attempt to create database automatically, but user must exist
Falls back to SQLite automatically - check console for "Using SQLite"
Create .env file with GHOST_ADMIN_EMAIL and GHOST_ADMIN_PASS
Add require('dotenv').config() at top of your entry file
Pass credentials programmatically: init({ adminEmail: '...', adminPassword: '...' })

symptoms.symptom: Dashboard UI loads but shows connection error

causes.cause: Dashboard server started but routes not mounted

solutions.solution: Check console for "Dashboard server started" message
Verify dashboard accessible: curl http://localhost:3001/api/auth/setup-status
Check browser console for CORS errors

symptoms.symptom: Requests pass through without DNA header

causes.cause: Path doesn't match middleware mount point

solutions.solution: Ensure init() completes before calling secure(): use await or .then()
Check middleware order - ghosttrace.secure() must come before route handlers
Verify path: app.use('/api', secure()) only protects /api/* routes

symptoms.symptom: Node.js process memory grows over time

causes.cause: Too many behavioral profiles in memory
Rate limit map not being cleaned

solutions.solution: Behavioral profiles are automatically cleaned up after inactivity
Adjust NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 if needed
Consider using Redis for session storage in high-traffic scenarios

symptoms.symptom: Type errors when using ghosttrace in TypeScript project

solutions.solution: Verify index.d.ts exists in node_modules/ghosttrace/
Check tsconfig.json includes "moduleResolution": "node"
Import with: import ghosttrace from 'ghosttrace' or import * as ghosttrace from 'ghosttrace'

practice.title: Never commit credentials to version control
practice.description: Store GHOST_ADMIN_PASS and database credentials in .env file and add .env to .gitignore

practice.title: Use strong admin passwords
practice.description: Minimum 12 characters with mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols

practice.title: Adjust thresholds per route sensitivity
practice.description: Use lower thresholds (50-60) for authentication and payment routes, higher thresholds (80-90) for public read-only endpoints

practice.title: Use database connection pooling
practice.description: Configure connection pools for high-traffic scenarios

practice.title: Enable database indexing
practice.description: GhostTrace creates indexes automatically, but verify they exist for optimal query performance

practice.title: Monitor dashboard logs regularly
practice.description: Check for unusual patterns, failed login attempts, and system errors

practice.title: Set up incident response workflows
practice.description: Define procedures for critical alerts and integrate with existing SOC processes

practice.title: Test in monitor-only mode first
practice.description: Start with blockOnThreat: false to observe behavior before enabling blocking

practice.title: Gradually roll out protection
practice.description: Start with non-critical endpoints, tune thresholds, then expand to critical paths

practice.title: Enable audit logging for compliance
practice.description: Audit trail is automatic - export logs periodically for compliance reporting

practice.title: Configure AI provider fallback
practice.description: Set up multiple AI providers for redundancy in case primary fails
practice.example: Primary: OpenAI, Fallback: Anthropic Claude, Final fallback: Rule-based analysis

optimization-tips.tip: Enable Redis for session storage in high-traffic scenarios
Adjust rate limits based on traffic patterns
Run dashboard on separate server for large deployments
Use CDN for dashboard static assets in distributed setups
